title: SIGTERM kills requests still in flight
context_text: A rolling deploy terminates pods and long-running requests are cut off, surfacing as client-side 502s during every release
solution_text: Handle SIGTERM by stopping new work, draining in-flight requests, then exiting. Set the orchestrator's grace period longer than the slowest expected request.
source: public: Kubernetes pod termination lifecycle documentation

title: Readiness probe wired to a dependency check
context_text: A brief database outage makes every replica report unhealthy at once, so the orchestrator restarts them all and the outage gets worse
solution_text: Keep liveness independent of dependencies; only readiness should test them. A dependency being down means stop sending traffic, not restart the process.
source: public: Kubernetes probe documentation distinguishes liveness from readiness for exactly this reason

title: ADD COLUMN NOT NULL fails on a populated table
context_text: A migration that adds a non-nullable column succeeds on an empty test database and fails in production with 'column contains null values'
solution_text: Supply a server-side default so existing rows backfill, or add the column nullable, backfill, then set NOT NULL.
source: public: standard SQL DDL semantics; reproduced identically on PostgreSQL and MySQL

title: Schema migration locks a table during deploy
context_text: An index build or column rewrite takes an exclusive lock and blocks reads and writes for the duration on a large table
solution_text: Build indexes concurrently where the engine supports it, and split the change into expand, backfill, contract phases so the old and new application versions both work mid-migration.
source: public: PostgreSQL CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY documentation; expand/contract is standard practice

title: Docker layer cache invalidated by copying source too early
context_text: Every build reinstalls all dependencies because source files are copied before the dependency manifest, invalidating the cached layer
solution_text: Copy the dependency manifest and install first, then copy source. Ordering instructions from least to most frequently changed keeps the cache useful.
source: public: Docker documentation on build cache and layer invalidation

title: Secrets baked into an image layer
context_text: A credential passed as a build argument or copied in and later deleted is still recoverable from the image history
solution_text: Never pass secrets as build args or COPY them in. Inject at runtime from the platform's secret store, or use a build-time secret mount that leaves no layer.
source: public: Docker documentation warns that build args and deleted files persist in layer history

title: Container runs as root by default
context_text: A compromised process in the container has root in the namespace, widening the blast radius of any application-level vulnerability
solution_text: Create an unprivileged user in the image and switch to it with USER before the entrypoint. Drop capabilities the process does not need.
source: public: standard container-hardening guidance; CIS Docker Benchmark

title: Rate limiter state held per process
context_text: An in-memory rate limiter allows roughly N times the intended rate once the service runs on N replicas
solution_text: Hold the counter in a shared store with atomic increment and TTL, or enforce the limit at a gateway in front of the replicas.
source: public: standard consequence of local state in a horizontally scaled service
